question: A cylindrical rod has an outer curved surface area of 1800 cm² . If the length of the rod is 52 cm, then the outer radius (in cm) of the rod, correct to two places of decimal, is: Take pi=(22)/(7).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the direct formula for Curved Surface Area: CSA = 2πrh

⇒ Radius (r) = CSA ÷ (2 × π × h)

⇒ r = 1800 ÷ (2 × 22/7 × 52)

⇒ r = (1800 × 7) ÷ (44 × 52) = 12600 ÷ 2288

⇒ r ≈ 5.5069 cm ≈ 5.51 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 5.51 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Outer curved surface area of the cylindrical rod = 1800 cm²

Length (height, h) of the rod = 52 cm

π = 22/7

 h = 52 cm
 
 CSA = 1800 cm²

**Formula Used:**

Curved Surface Area of a cylinder = 2πrh

Where 'r' is the outer radius and 'h' is the length of the rod.

**Calculations:**

⇒ 2 × (22/7) × r × 52 = 1800

⇒ (44/7) × 52 × r = 1800

⇒ (2288/7) × r = 1800

⇒ r = (1800 × 7) ÷ 2288

⇒ r = 12600 ÷ 2288

⇒ r ≈ 5.5069 cm

Rounding off to two decimal places, we get r = 5.51 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 5.51 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Curved Surface Area (CSA)

It is the area of the lateral surface excluding the circular bases. Formula: CSA = 2πrh.

Total Surface Area (TSA)

It includes the curved surface area along with the area of the top and bottom circular bases. Formula: TSA = 2πr(h + r).

Volume of a Cylinder

It represents the total capacity inside the standard cylinder. Formula: Volume = πr²h.
